_about: Seed for the incident clocks in Rulebook in Motion. Each regime lists the steps an organisation must report, the time limit and the event the clock starts from. All values are leads from working knowledge and Swann's drafts; confirm each against the article text on EUR-Lex, quote the sentence that sets the limit, and record the CELEX and paragraph before setting verify to false.

regimes.who: Essential and important entities, for significant incidents

steps.label: Early warning
steps.from: becoming aware of the significant incident

steps.label: Incident notification
steps.from: becoming aware of the significant incident

regimes.notes: Intermediate reports on request are not timed. Article 23(9) quarterly summary to ENISA is anonymised and aggregated.

regimes.who: Critical entities designated by a Member State

steps.label: Notification
steps.from: becoming aware of the incident, unless operationally unable

regimes.notes: Applies only to entities a Member State has designated; the tool cannot decide designation.

regimes.who: Manufacturers of products with digital elements, for actively exploited vulnerabilities

steps.label: Early warning
steps.from: becoming aware of the actively exploited vulnerability

steps.label: Final report
steps.from: a corrective or mitigating measure becoming available

regimes.notes: Reports go through the single reporting platform to the CSIRT coordinator and ENISA. Confirm the application date in Article 71.

regimes.who: Manufacturers of products with digital elements, for severe incidents affecting product security

steps.label: Early warning
steps.from: becoming aware of the severe incident

regimes.instrument: DORA Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 with its delegated rules on incident reporting
regimes.article: Article 19 and the delegated act setting time limits
regimes.who: Financial entities, for major ICT-related incidents

steps.label: Initial notification
steps.from: classification of the incident as major, and no later than 24 hours from becoming aware

regimes.notes: The time limits sit in a delegated or implementing act rather than in Article 19 itself. Resolve which act and record its CELEX.

steps.label: Notification to the supervisory authority
steps.from: becoming aware of the breach, where feasible

regimes.notes: Not required where the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to rights and freedoms.

regimes.who: Providers of high-risk AI systems, for serious incidents

steps.label: Serious incident report
steps.from: becoming aware of the serious incident

steps.label: Report, widespread infringement or critical infrastructure disruption

regimes.notes: The application date for high-risk obligations may have been moved by the Digital Omnibus on AI. Resolve the current date before showing this regime at all; if unresolved, hide it and say why.
